headline: Nvidia fades after its beat and Fed minutes bite: Dow −1.1%, S&P −0.2%, Nasdaq +0.4%
summary: Stocks opened higher on Nvidia's beat-and-raise, but the gains faded as the chipmaker reversed lower and the S&P 500 slipped back into the red after the 2 p.m. Fed minutes, leaving it with a fifth straight loss, its longest losing streak since June. The rotation underneath was stark: the Dow lost 561 points on health insurers, energy and miners, while the Nasdaq snapped its losing run on cybersecurity, retail and selected chip gains and the Russell 2000 rose 0.5%.
drivers: Nvidia was up about 4% before the open after beating estimates, guiding Q4 to $130B and lifting its next-year growth outlook to 75% plus a bigger buyback, but it closed −2.9% at $150.96 as leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit weighed. Chips split: AMD +5.3% and Broadcom +3.6%, while Micron (−1.0%) and Intel (−0.9%) slipped.
Health insurers and defensives sink the Dow
UnitedHealth fell 10.2% and Humana about 13% on worries over tougher regulatory scrutiny of insurers, with Merck −3.9%, Amgen −3.1% and Caterpillar −2.1% adding to the Dow's 561-point drop.
Commodity slide hits energy and miners

WTI fell 3.2% to $83.26, its lowest since late August, after a surprise 3.4M-barrel US crude build, dragging the S&P energy sector down about 3.5% (Chevron −4.0%, refiners about −5%); copper fell about 6% and gold about 3.5%, sending Freeport-McMoRan and Newmont down more than 6%.
Hawkish Fed minutes, but lower yields

The October minutes showed almost all officials expect further hikes and a few open to a 50bp move in December if inflation data disappoint, which knocked the S&P off its highs; the oil slide still pulled the 10-year yield down about 4bp to 5.07%, and the VIX eased 3.5%. Anthropic priced its IPO after the close at $83, above its $70–78 range, while cybersecurity (Palo Alto +10%, CrowdStrike +8%) and retailers TJX (+8%) and Target (+4%) on earnings beats propped up the Nasdaq.
week: Three sessions in, the S&P 500 is down 3.1%, the Nasdaq 2.8%, the Dow 4.1% and the Russell 2000 2.7% for the week, with the 10-year yield still above 5% and a December Fed hike almost fully priced.
watch: Next: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut under ANT and Walmart's results on Thu Nov 19, the December WTI contract expiry on Fri Nov 20, and the Fed meeting on Dec 8–9.
